newsitem.title: CUBA: Hurricane Lili hurts Cuban agriculture.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili hurts Cuban agriculture.

text.p: Cuba counted the cost of damage from Hurricane Lili on Saturday, with authorities saying the storm caused widespread damage to crops including citrus fruits and bananas.

No overall figures were issued for damage by the hurricane, which swept over central and western areas of the communist-ruled island on Thursday night and on Friday before heading northeast for the Bahamas.

There were no casualties reported but about 7,000 homes were damaged, most of them partially, state media said. Some areas of central Cuba were still without power on Saturday. Power was restored to most parts of Havana late on Friday.
Farm workers on the Isle of Youth to the south of mainland Cuba were rushing to recover 15,000 tons of citrus fruits blown to the ground by the storm.
In Havana province, there was considerable damage to banana plantations. Citrus plantations in Jaguey Grande in neighboring Matanzas were also hurt, but no figures were given.

In Cienfuegos province, badly affected by the hurricane, many roads were cut by fallen trees and local authorities reported damage to coffee, citrus plantations and bananas. Total damage to sugar cane, due to be harvested in two or three months, was not yet given.
International flights to and from Cuba, suspended late on Thursday, were resumed on Friday afternoon.

Hurricane Lili caused wind gusts of up to 110 mph (180 kph) in Cienfuegos and dumped torrential rains over much of the country. The heaviest rainfall was 17 inches (43 cm) in 24 hours recorded at Topes de Collantes in the Escambray mountains east of Cienfuegos.
